correctness.rationale: For real 1<=p<infinity, p!=2, the strict scalar Clarkson inequality at overlapping nonzero coordinates plus ||u_i±u_j||_p^p=2 proves all column supports disjoint; at p=1 strict negative sign still holds. Exactly one output row is unused, so one column may occupy two coordinates and no more. Fixed-sign arcs |a|^p+|b|^p=1 attach between signed singleton-support injections; endpoints, continuity and compact-Hausdorff argument give a finite graph, with 2^(n-1)n! vertices and 2(n-1) neighbors per vertex. The even-signed W(D_n) extension and star-transposition generators ensure connectedness. Thus E=(n-1)V and pi1 free of rank 1+(n-2)V. The standard four-arc planar loop survives Euclidean normalization to generator of pi1(SO(n)), including n=2 circle and n>=3 order-two cases. Independent exact graph reconstruction checked n=2..5: (V,E,b1)=(4,4,1),(24,48,25),(192,576,385),(1920,7680,5761). Bounded checks corroborate the all-n mathematical proof rather than imply it.
